items.title: Section: Fascicle 48 Opens — The Ten Minds Carried Forward From Utmost Joy, Now Fully Ripened

items.zh: 問：增上戒住菩薩轉時，當知何行、何狀、何相？答：若諸菩薩，先於極歡喜住，由十種心意樂，已得意樂清淨。何等為十？一者、於一切師長尊重福田，不行虛誑意樂；二者、於同法菩薩忍辱柔和，易可共住意樂；三者、勝伏一切煩惱及隨煩惱眾魔事業，心自在轉意樂；四者、於一切行深見過失意樂；五者、於大涅槃深見勝利意樂；六者、於諸妙善菩提分法，常勤修習意樂；七者、即於彼修為隨順故，樂處遠離意樂；八者、於諸世間有染尊位利養恭敬，無所顧戀意樂；九者、遠離下乘，趣證大乘意樂；十者、欲作一切有情一切義利意樂。
items.en:
Within the Basic Section, the Bodhisattva Stage, the second yoga foundation of sustained practice, the chapter on the abodes, part two.
Third abode, heightened discipline; first, the question. Question: when a bodhisattva at the abode of heightened discipline turns, what conduct, what state, what mark should be understood?
Second, the answer; first, the brief account; first, distinguishing each mark; first, purified aspiration; first, presenting the aspiration; first, naming it. Answer: if bodhisattvas, previously at the abode of utmost joy, through ten kinds of mind-aspiration, had already attained purified aspiration —
Second, posing the question. What are the ten?
Third, listing them. First, a mind free of all deception towards every teacher and elder, a genuine field of merit. Second, a mind of patient forbearance and gentleness, easily dwelling together with fellow bodhisattvas of the same dharma. Third, a mind sovereign over every affliction, secondary affliction, and the undertakings of every demonic force. Fourth, a mind that sees deeply into the faults of all conditioned activity. Fifth, a mind that sees deeply into great nirvana's own excellent benefit. Sixth, a mind constantly, diligently cultivating the wondrously excellent factors of awakening. Seventh, according with that very cultivation, a mind delighting in dwelling in solitude. Eighth, a mind entirely without longing towards the world's own tainted status, gain, and reverence. Ninth, a mind departed from the lesser vehicles, oriented towards realising the great vehicle. Tenth, a mind wishing to accomplish every kind of benefit for every sentient being.

items.title: Section: These Ten Undistorted Minds Together Are Called Purified Aspiration

items.zh: 如是十種無倒意樂依心而轉，是故說為意樂清淨。
items.en:
Second, clarifying purity. These ten kinds of undistorted mind, continuously turning and depending on the mind, are for this reason called purified aspiration.
Commentary: Regarding "these ten kinds of undistorted mind" and the like — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: if a bodhisattva, having already fully accomplished the first ground, wishes to attain the second ground, ten kinds of straightforward mind should arise. What are the ten? First, straightforward mind. Second, gentle mind. Third, tamed mind. Fourth, wholesome mind. Fifth, quiescent mind. Sixth, genuine mind. Seventh, unmixed mind. Eighth, undesiring mind. Ninth, superior mind. Tenth, great mind. A bodhisattva giving rise to these ten minds is able to enter the second bodhisattva ground, the ground free of stain. The ten kinds of undistorted aspiration here should be understood to correspond in this very order.

items.title: Section: Innate Precept-Fulfilment, and Freedom From Even the Slightest Violation

items.zh: 即由如是十種意樂成上品故，極圓滿故，是諸菩薩入證第二增上戒住。於此住中，性戒具足。極少邪惡業道所攝諸惡犯戒尚不現行，況中上品。又於十種圓滿業道，自性顯現。
items.en:
Second, innate precept-fulfilment. Precisely because these ten kinds of aspiration have become of the most excellent grade, utterly complete, such bodhisattvas enter and are certified into the second abode of heightened discipline. Within this abode, precepts of their own inherent nature are fulfilled.
Third, freedom from every violation. Even the very slightest evil conduct subsumed within a wrongful course of karmic action, violating the precepts, does not manifest at all — let alone conduct of a middling or superior grade. Furthermore, regarding the ten kinds of perfected course of karmic action, these manifest of their own inherent nature.
Commentary: Regarding "from innate precept-fulfilment to manifesting of their own inherent nature" — this concerns the purity of restraint-precepts, one should understand. Departing from killing all the way through departing from wrong view are called the ten kinds of perfected course of karmic action. Manifesting purely within these courses of karmic action, without recourse to deliberate discrimination, is called manifesting of their own inherent nature.

items.title: Section: Thorough Understanding of Cause and Fruit, Ripening-Fruit and Outflow-Fruit

items.zh: 菩薩如是性戒具足，能以妙慧，於染不染、惡趣善趣，及諸乘中諸業現行、若因若果、修證安立，如實了知。於異熟果及等流果如是諸業，如實了知。
items.en:
Fourth, thoroughly understanding karma and its course; first, regarding cause and fruit. Bodhisattvas, precepts of their own inherent nature thus fulfilled, are able, with wondrous wisdom, to genuinely know exactly as it is whatever pertains to tainted or untainted conduct, unfortunate or fortunate rebirth, and karmic action currently manifesting across every vehicle, together with cause, fruit, and how cultivation and realisation are established.
Second, regarding the course of karmic action. Regarding the ripening-fruit and the outflow-fruit belonging to these very actions, one genuinely knows exactly as it is.

items.title: Section: Personally Practising Pure Karma, and Delighting in Encouraging Others to Do the Same

items.zh: 自能現斷諸不善業，自能現受一切善業。即於其中樂勸導他，能正勸導。
items.en:
Fifth, receiving and practising pure karma; first, personally able to receive it. Personally able to presently sever every unwholesome karma, personally able to presently receive every wholesome karma.
Second, delighting in encouraging others. Precisely within this same practice, delighting in guiding others towards it, able to guide them correctly.
Commentary: Regarding "with wondrous wisdom" through "able to guide correctly" — this concerns the purity of the precepts gathering wholesome dharma, one should understand. "Cause" means tainted or untainted. "Fruit" means unfortunate or fortunate rebirth. "Cultivation and realisation" means regarding the vehicles. "Established in teaching" means the very distinctions of the four noble truths. All of this is genuinely known. Furthermore, regarding karma yielding ripening-fruit and outflow-fruit, this too is genuinely known. Personally able to depart from unwholesome courses of karmic action, abiding in wholesome courses; likewise causing others to correctly depart, correctly abide — this is why one delights in guiding others, able to guide them correctly.

items.title: Section: Great Compassion for Beings Steeped in Ultimate Suffering, Whatever Their Worldly Fortune

items.zh: 於其種種不平等業現行過失之所染污諸有情界，若興若衰，等無差別，一切皆墮第一義苦，並住艱辛，種種艱辛之所逼切，甚可哀愍。於彼獲得廣大哀愍，如實觀照。
items.en:
Sixth, compassionate regard for suffering beings. Towards the realm of sentient beings, defiled by the fault of manifesting every kind of unequal karmic action, whether flourishing or declining, equally without distinction, all fall entirely into the suffering of ultimate truth, abiding amid hardship, pressed upon by every kind of difficulty — profoundly deserving of compassion. Towards them, one attains vast compassion, observing this truly, exactly as it is.
Commentary: Regarding "towards the realm of sentient beings" through "observing this truly, exactly as it is" — this concerns the purity of the precepts benefiting sentient beings, one should understand. The suffering of the five aggregates of grasping is called the suffering of ultimate truth. The immeasurable distinctions of hardship in being born are as explained in the stage with both examination and analysis (fascicle 9, page 677 of the Nanjing edition). One should understand "pressed upon by every kind of difficulty" accordingly.

items.title: Section: Purified Wholesome Roots — Gold Refined Further Still in Alum, Explaining the Name "Ground Free of Stain"

items.zh: 是諸菩薩安住如是增上戒住，廣見諸佛、善根清淨，如前應知。此差別者，謂如世間善巧工匠，以所鍊金置迦肆娑，置於火中數數燒鍊，轉更明淨。如是菩薩善根清淨，當知亦爾。
items.en:
Seventh, purified wholesome roots; first, pointing to what was already said. Bodhisattvas abiding in this abode of heightened discipline likewise broadly behold the buddhas, wholesome roots purified, exactly as already explained.
Second, a simile marking the difference. The difference is this: just as, in the world, a skilful craftsman takes gold already refined and places it in alum, and, placed in fire, smelted again and again, it becomes ever more bright and pure — so too should a bodhisattva's own purified wholesome roots be understood, just so.

items.title: Section: Rebirth as a Gold-Wheel King, and Majestic Power Tenfold Greater Than the First Ground's Own

items.zh: 於此住中，淨心意樂成滿趣入。在所生處多作輪王，王四大洲。以自在力，令多有情止息犯戒不善業道，勸彼受行諸善業道。當知威力過前十倍。
items.en:
Eighth, rebirth. Within this abode, purified aspiration having reached complete fulfilment, one attains entry. In whatever place of rebirth, one most often becomes a wheel-turning king, ruling four great continents. With sovereign power, causing many sentient beings to cease precept-violating, unwholesome courses of karmic action, encouraging them to undertake wholesome courses of karmic action.
Ninth, majestic power. One should understand that majestic power exceeds the previous ground's own tenfold.

items.title: Section: The Summary Names All Nine Aspects, and the Treatise Confirms — Heightened Discipline Is the Ground Free of Stain

items.zh: 當知是名略說菩薩增上戒住。謂意樂淨故；性戒具足故；離一切種毀犯戒垢故；一切業道、一切因果了知通達故；於諸淨業能自受行，亦樂勸他令其受行故；於有情界諸業所生眾苦艱辛，得大哀愍，如實觀照故；善根清淨故；受生故；威力故。若廣宣說，如十地經離垢地說。遠離一切犯戒垢故，名離垢地。由離一切犯戒垢故，即此名為增上戒住。彼離垢地，當知即此增上戒住。
items.en:
Second, closing the brief meaning. One should understand this, in brief, as the bodhisattva's abode of heightened discipline — namely, because of purified aspiration; because innate precepts are fulfilled; because every kind of precept-violating stain is departed from; because every course of karmic action and every cause and fruit are genuinely understood and penetrated; because pure karma is personally practised, and others are delighted in being encouraged to undertake it; because vast compassion is attained towards the many sufferings and hardships arising from karmic action across the realm of sentient beings, truly observed exactly as it is; because of purified wholesome roots; because of rebirth; because of majestic power.
Second, the broader pointer; first, pointing to it. Should one wish to hear it expounded at length, it is exactly as the Ten Grounds Sutra expounds it in its chapter on the ground free of stain.
Second, the correspondence. Because every stain of precept-violation is departed from entirely, it is named the ground free of stain. Because of this very freedom from every stain of precept-violation, this is called the abode of heightened discipline. One should understand that ground free of stain is exactly this abode of heightened discipline.

items.title: Section: The Abode of Heightened Mind Opens — Ten Further Kinds of Purified-Mind Reflection, the First Five Named

items.zh: 問：增上心住菩薩轉時，當知何行、何狀、何相？答：若諸菩薩，先於增上戒住，已得十種清淨意樂，作意思惟解了通達。復由餘十淨心意樂作意思惟成上品故，極圓滿故，過增上戒住，入增上心住。何等為十？一者、作意思惟：我於十種淨心意樂已得清淨；二者、作意思惟：我於十種淨心意樂已清淨故，能不退失；三者、作意思惟：我於一切漏有漏法心不趣入，於違背中能正安住；四者、作意思惟：我能於彼修對治中，識正安住；五者、作意思惟：我能於彼所修對治，不復退失；
items.en:
Fourth abode, heightened mind; first, the question. Question: when a bodhisattva at the abode of heightened mind turns, what conduct, what state, what mark should be understood?
Second, the answer; first, the brief account; first, distinguishing each mark; first, purified-mind reflection bringing entry to fulfilment; first, naming it. Answer: if bodhisattvas, previously at the abode of heightened discipline, having already attained ten kinds of purified aspiration, reflected upon and thoroughly penetrated them — further, by ten other kinds of purified-mind aspiration and reflection becoming of the most excellent grade, utterly complete, one passes beyond the abode of heightened discipline and enters the abode of heightened mind.
Second, posing the question. What are the ten?
Third, listing them. First, reflecting: the ten kinds of purified-mind aspiration have themselves already become pure. Second, reflecting: because the ten kinds of purified-mind aspiration have already become pure, they are able not to regress. Third, reflecting: towards every contaminated and defiling dharma, the mind does not enter at all, abiding correctly amid what opposes it. Fourth, reflecting: within cultivating the remedy for these, consciousness abides correctly. Fifth, reflecting: within this remedy already cultivated, one does not regress from it.

blocks.text: Fascicle 48 continues the abodes, one ground at a time. Each ground is described in the same pattern: its aspirations, its practice, a simile of gold being refined, the kind of rebirth it brings, and its power. Today: the second ground.

"First, the aspiration never to deceive any teacher, honoured one, or field of merit; second, patience and gentleness, easy to live with, towards fellow bodhisattvas." Venerable Miào Jìng: no scheming, no thought of "let me tell him a little lie". Master Cháng Bǎi: living together is as comfortable as a spring breeze brushing the face.
Master Cháng Bǎi: "the straight mind is the place of awakening": upright, never deceiving teachers. Venerable Miào Jìng: the first aspiration is the straight mind.
Venerable Miào Jìng: good has become your nature; when your mind stirs, it is good, without forcing.

Venerable Miào Jìng: an outflow result resembles its cause: kill and your life will be short; release life and it will be long. Master Cháng Bǎi: in a ripening result, the cause is good or evil while the result itself is neutral.

Venerable Miào Jìng: all are equally suffering beings, even those who do good; ultimate suffering is that of the five grasped aggregates. (Ru-Yi reads this as worldly fortune; the lecturers read it as ultimate suffering.)

"A skilled craftsman places refined gold in alum and smelts it again and again until it is brighter." Master Cháng Bǎi: the alum removes impurities. Venerable Miào Jìng: faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom are purified the same way.
Venerable Miào Jìng: the first-ground bodhisattva rules only Jambudvīpa; the second rules four continents, as a gold-wheel king.
"Free of every stain of precept-violation, it is called the Stainless Ground." Master Cháng Bǎi: neither deliberate nor accidental violation.
"First, reflecting: I have attained purity in the ten purified-mind aspirations." Venerable Miào Jìng: "reflecting" here really means practising calm and insight.
"Easy to live with." It is listed second of ten, right after honesty. For both teachers, this ordinary virtue is the sign of a real bodhisattva.

quiz.q: What is the first of the ten aspirations leading into the abode of heightened discipline?
options: never deceiving teachers, the honoured, and fields of merit
quiz.why: "First, the aspiration never to deceive any teacher, honoured one, or field of merit; second, patience and gentleness, easy to live with, towards fellow bodhisattvas." Venerable Miào Jìng: no scheming, no thought of "let me tell him a little lie."

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe the second — "easy to live with among fellow bodhisattvas"?
options: living together is as pleasant as a spring breeze on the face
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: living together is as comfortable as a spring breeze brushing the face.

quiz.q: How do these ten aspirations match the Ten Grounds Sūtra's ten "straight minds"? What do the lectures say of the first?
options: both: the first, non-deceiving aspiration, is the "straight mind" — Cháng Bǎi cites "the straight mind is the place of awakening"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "the straight mind is the place of awakening" — upright, without crooked discrimination, never deceiving teachers. Venerable Miào Jìng: the first aspiration is the straight mind.

quiz.q: "The ten perfected courses of action manifest by their own nature." How do the lectures explain this?
options: both: pure spontaneously without deliberation — Cháng Bǎi: unlike ordinary people's inner battles; Miào Jìng: goodness has become one's nature
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: unlike ordinary people who must struggle between good and evil, it is pure without deliberation — that is manifesting by its own nature. Venerable Miào Jìng: good has become your nature; when your mind stirs, it is good, without forcing.

quiz.q: Regarding "ripening-fruit and outflow-fruit," what is the outflow-fruit?
options: the fruit resembles the cause — killing brings short life, releasing life long life
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: outflow means the fruit resembles the cause — kill and your life will be short; release life and it will be long. Master Cháng Bǎi: in ripening-fruit the cause is good or evil while the fruit is neutral.

quiz.q: "Whether flourishing or declining, all fall into ultimate suffering." The English reads 興衰 as worldly fortune. How do the lectures read it?
options: Miào Jìng: even those doing good are suffering beings; ultimate suffering is the five grasped aggregates; Cháng Bǎi: as long as one wanders in the three realms, it is suffering
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: all are equally suffering beings — even those who do good; ultimate suffering is that of the five grasped aggregates. Master Cháng Bǎi: from the ultimate view, as long as there is karmic result and wandering in the three realms, it is suffering. The English reads it as worldly fortune.

quiz.q: In the second ground's simile, refined gold is placed in what and smelted again?
options: alum, then smelted again and again until brighter
quiz.why: "A skilful craftsman places refined gold in alum and smelts it again and again until brighter." Master Cháng Bǎi: the alum removes impurities. Venerable Miào Jìng: the roots of faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom are purified the same way.

quiz.q: At the second ground one often becomes a king "ruling four continents." How do the lectures compare the first and second grounds?
options: both: first ground, iron-wheel king of one continent; second ground, gold-wheel king of four — ten times the power
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: first-ground bodhisattvas rule one continent as iron-wheel kings; second-ground ones mostly become gold-wheel kings. Venerable Miào Jìng: the first rules only Jambudvīpa, the second four continents — a gold-wheel king.

quiz.q: What is the abode of heightened discipline called in the Ten Grounds Sūtra, and why?
options: Stainless — free of every stain of precept-breaking
quiz.why: "Free of every stain of precept-violation, it is called the Stainless Ground — the same as the abode of heightened discipline." Master Cháng Bǎi: neither deliberate nor accidental violation.

quiz.q: In the ten purified-mind reflections leading into heightened mind, what is the first?
options: "I have attained purity in the ten purified-mind aspirations"
quiz.why: "First, reflecting: I have attained purity in the ten purified-mind aspirations; second, having purified them, I won't regress." Venerable Miào Jìng: "reflecting" here really means practising calm and insight.
